translation: The Ci Zhi Lun states: "With vacuous qi and bodily heat, [it is] obtained from injury by summerheat; this is heat wounding the qi." The Wei Lun states: "When one travels far and is toil-weary, and encounters great heat and is thirsty, the yang qi attacks from within; when it attacks from within, heat lodges in the kidney. The kidney is the water viscus; now, since water cannot conquer fire, the bones become withered and the marrow vacuous, the feet cannot sustain the body, and bone-wilting [wei] develops." Hence the lower [section of the] Classic says: "Bone-wilting is born from great heat." This is dampness-heat forming wilting, and makes a person's bones depleted and strengthless. Therefore in treating wilting one alone takes the yangming [channel]. When the season reaches long summer, dampness-heat greatly conquers, steaming and blazing into the person; those who are affected mostly have fatigue and weariness of the four limbs, scantness of spirit, laziness toward movement, fullness of the chest, hurried respiration, heaviness and pain of the limbs and joints, or qi being high and wheezing, bodily heat and vexation, [pulse-]box distension below the heart [epigastrium], urine yellow and scant, stool loose and frequent, or diarrhea issuing yellow lees, or like the color of rice-wash, or thirst or no thirst, no desire for food and drink, spontaneous sweating, heavy body, or scant sweat — [in this] the blood is diseased first and the qi is not diseased. In its pulse is obtained surging and moderate; if damp qi is mutually struggling, it must further add slowness [遲]. Although the slow pulse [遲] and intermittent [disease] may interchange and differ slightly, its Heavenly summer-heat and damp command [disease] are one and the same. One should use cooling-decanting medicinals to treat it. I name it Qingshu Yiqi Tang (Clears-Summerheat Augments-Qi Decoction), and it governs.
